National Laboratory of the Rockies | 18 Some factors are more difficult to capture in nationally representative data but impact siting decisions • Vacancy rates1—e.g., investors may be more confident financing projects in top-tier markets with low vacancy rates • Electricity rates and grid costs, supply chain issues, and other input costs and trends • Lessons from Northern Virginia, Texas, and other regions with clustered data center development show that qualitative factors have the potential to impact investment and siting decisions. ◦ Zoning and permitting laws ◦ Local and state tax laws and incentives2—tax breaks for data center developers ◦ Public support and/or opposition3 ◦ Local workforce composition2—e.g., for data-center-specific jobs and having a sufficient workforce to staff the data center.
